questions.question: What shows you how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?

options.text: The supply pressure gauge
The ABS malfunction lamp
The tractor protection valve

questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in the vehicle's air tanks.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Get upset.
Accept it and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Always drive safely.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always good.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
To stay slower than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery surfaces. Too much power can cause your vehicle to lose control.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should the heaviest cargo be placed?

options.text: On top of the lightest cargo.
Under the lightest cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under the lightest cargo.
questions.explanation: Avoid making vehicles top-heavy. Top-heavy vehicles are more likely to roll over. Place heavy cargo underneath lighter cargo.

questions.question: What does ABS allow a driver to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up. It helps you maintain control when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: Can be exceeded in cooler conditions.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
Must be written in the shipping papers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely hold at a given pressure. This rating is shown on the side of the tire.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
Aim at the flames.
Use any extinguisher on every type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. Only use water on certain fires. If you are unsure, wait for trained firefighters.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. It is used to watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: You must stop.
You may proceed without stopping.
You must wait for the light to turn yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed without stopping.
questions.explanation: When a drawbridge has a green traffic light, you do not need to stop. However, slow down before crossing to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Holds the cargo in a large box
Prevents cargo from sliding during transport
Prevents others from buying the cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents cargo from sliding during transport
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from moving during transport.

questions.question: Why should you check tires regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure goes up when temperature rises. You should check tire pressure and mounting carefully when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: How should you park to make it easier to leave?

options.text: Park so you can back up when leaving.
Park so you can drive forward when leaving.
Park only on the side of roads, not in parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park so you can drive forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky and should be avoided. Park in a space where you can drive forward when you leave.

questions.question: What happens when cargo has a high center of gravity?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to roll over.
Items are more likely to fall down.
It becomes harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Loading cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Cargo should be loaded evenly and safely.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, what should the coolant temperature do?

options.text: Decrease.
Rise slowly.
Jump quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, coolant temperature should rise gradually to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in a vehicle?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Only during interstate travel.
Yes, it is required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that your vehicle has emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is the horn used for?

options.text: To show other drivers that you are angry.
To warn other drivers that you are nearby.
To frighten other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: The horn warns others that you are near. Use it only when needed, since it can startle other drivers and cause danger.

questions.question: How do you know if a vehicle can handle a load?

options.text: Know the vehicle's suspension rating.
Know the tire rating for the front tires only.
Start driving and see how the vehicle performs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension weight capacity.

questions.question: Is it safe to reach unsafely for a phone while driving?

options.text: Yes, if you are driving alone.
Yes, if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
No, not even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, not even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
questions.explanation: If you use a phone while driving, it must be close and easily reachable without taking your hands off the wheel. Unsafe reaching for a phone is dangerous and against the rules, even if you plan to use hands-free mode.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?

options.text: Compressed air
Outside air
Non-compressed air

questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often use air brakes. Air brake systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people if cargo spills
To protect cargo from weather
To keep the cargo secret

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep the cargo secret
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people from spills and to protect the cargo from weather. Keeping cargo secret is not a reason to cover it.
